thread:
maria_s: heads-up — AcmeCo private (VPC) reported bursts of 403s and huge p95 (300-800ms). They say traffic from their VPC is being handled in us-west instead of eu-west. Possibly wrong egress selection / peering.

support-bot: ticket created #INC-4821, priority=P2.

alex_k: do you have a short repro + request headers? also what's their egress SNAT IP?

maria_s: repro below, customer replaced IDs for privacy. curl shows region header mismatch and auth failure.

```
# repro (from customer's bastion in eu-spoke)
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.internal (34.56.78.90) port 443
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood-inference.internal
> Authorization: Bearer <token>
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-final-region: us-west-2
< x-request-id: req_abc123
< content-type: application/json
{ "error": "token-region-mismatch: token issued for eu-west-1" }
```

maria_s: traceroute from bastion -> our hostname shows hops toward transit hub in us-east then next hop goes to a proxy in us-west:

```
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.internal (34.56.78.90), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.7 ms
 2  10.254.1.1  5.2 ms
 3  transit-hub-eu (52.14.10.2)  15.8 ms
 4  transit-core (3.120.22.5)  48.3 ms
 5  proxy-egress-us-west (18.80.33.100)  130.6 ms
 6  api.redwood-inference.internal (34.56.78.90)  131.0 ms
```

samir_n: that looks like a route/policy issue on their transit hub (or our peering mapping). Two likely causes: (1) SNAT on their edge or hub maps traffic to a public IP that our routing policy prefers to send to us-west; (2) proxy upstream order picks us-west endpoint due to IP geolocation.

samir_n: quick checks to run on their hub: `ip route get 34.56.78.90`, `sudo iptables -t nat -L -n --line-numbers`, and BGP `show ip bgp summary` on the transit. Also tcpdump for 34.56.78.90 to see next-hop.

ellie_p: customer provided NAT mapping: their egress SNAT 54.210.11.22 is listed in our peering table as associated with us-west because a previous peering advert leaked that prefix toward us-west peer.

alex_k: if the prefix was advertised toward a different colo/peer, our frontend may route that ASN space to the wrong region. Can they show the BGP advertisements? ask for `show ip bgp 54.210.11.22` and route origin.

maria_s: paste from them below:

```
# from customer transit
show ip bgp 54.210.11.22
BGP table version is 21345, local router id 10.254.1.1
54.210.11.22/32, path: 65010 i, localpref 100
  -> via peer 203.0.113.9 (us-west-provider) origin igp
```

samir_n: there it is — that /32 is being seen via their us-west provider peer. Essentially their SD-WAN selects an upstream that advertises that NAT IP into our fabric on the us-west plane. Result: our smart-routing picks the us-west pool for that source.

jon_b: short-term workaround for customer: change SNAT IP to a prefix announced into eu peers (or remove NAT and use routed egress), or add policy on their transit to prefer eu upstream for destinations to api.redwood-inference.internal (34.56.78.90).

jon_b: we can also add a routing override on our side for that specific SNAT prefix to prefer eu endpoints, but that's invasive and needs approval.

maria_s: customer tried a workaround: forced egress via 10.2.0.1 (eu egress gw) and the calls return 200 and the x-final-region header shows eu-west-1. So changing egress path fixes it.

alex_k: can you attach packet capture from customer when it goes wrong (tcpdump -n host 34.56.78.90 and port 443) and include SNI/tls server hello? we want to confirm which frontend accepted the connection.

maria_s: attached pcap excerpt (they uploaded to the ticket). Capture shows SYN -> proxy-egress-us-west (18.80.33.100) and TLS SNI `api.redwood-inference.internal`. Frontend logs show request routed to us-west pool id `pool-usw-3`.

ellie_p: root cause summary: customer's SNAT IP was learned via a BGP session to a us-west provider, causing our global routing to classify that source as us-west-local, and proxy selection picked us-west backends (auth tokens scoped to eu failed).

samir_n: remediation options: (A) customer fixes announcement (stop advertising SNAT via us-west peer) — recommended; (B) customer remaps SNAT to eu-advertised prefix; (C) we add a temporary override so that requests originating from 54.210.11.22 are routed to eu pool (ops + network review required).

maria_s: customer asks for a temp fix on our side while they change their transit. can SRE/Network approve a targeted override?

opsbot: incident INC-4821 updated: escalation to eng-network and sre. Assigning samir_n and jon_b.

samir_n: ok I will draft the override request. we need: exact SNAT prefixes, desired target region (eu-west-1), and duration. also add monitoring to ensure no traffic steal.

maria_s: providing details in the ticket now. thanks all :thumbsup:

support-bot: note: follow up checklist added to INC-4821 — verify token mappings, add a canary route, notify customer when done.

maria_s: marking as escalated to network. will post updates here when we have the override ticket + ETA.
